title: Sustained Administration of β-cell Mitogens to Intact Mouse Islets Ex Vivo Using Biodegradable Poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) Microspheres
protocol: Label COI with a fluorescent dye that reacts with free primary amine.
Dissolve fluorophore in 200 µl of DMSO, using an 8x molar excess relative to moles of COI.
Resuspend 50 mg of COI up to a final volume of 800 µl in vehicle solution (62.5 ng/µl).
Add fluorophore/DMSO solution to the resuspended COI and vortex overnight at 4 °C.
Alternatively, vortex reaction mixture for 4 hr at room temperature.
Remove excess fluorophore using a desalting column after labeling.
Drain storage buffer from desalting column and rinse with 16 ml of deionized water.
Add fluorescently labeled COI to the desalting column.
Elute with 1.2 ml of deionized water and collect flow through as a separate sample.
Repeat elution step four additional times, each time adding 1.2 ml of deionized water.
Freeze all collected flow through samples at -80 °C.
Lyophilize frozen samples according to manufacturer's instructions for 24 hr.
Add 1 mg of fluorescently labeled COI to 100 μl of deionized water to form W1 phase.
Dissolve 65 mg of PLGA in 750 µl of dichloromethane and ultrasonicate for 10-30 seconds at 160 W to form the oil phase (O).
Add W1 phase drop-wise to the O phase and emulsify using a hand-held homogenizer at 20,000 rpm for 30 seconds.
Emulsify the resulting W1/O phase drop-wise into 15 ml of a 1% aqueous PVA solution using a hand-held homogenizer at 20,000 rpm for 30 seconds.
Transfer the emulsion to a 200 ml round-bottom flask and subject it to a 635 mm Hg vacuum in a rotary evaporator for 1 hour to remove solvent.
Aliquot 1 ml of the resulting aqueous phase into fourteen microcentrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge the aqueous solution at 7,500 x g for 8 minutes.
Remove 900 µl of aqueous solution from the microcentrifuge tubes using a micropipette.
Add 1 ml deionized water to each microcentrifuge tube to wash the microspheres.
Centrifuge at 7,500 x g for 8 minutes.
Carefully remove another 900 µl of aqueous solution from the microcentrifuge tubes using a micropipette.
Freeze the remaining 100 μl aqueous solution containing the generated microspheres at -80°C.
Lyophilize microspheres according to the manufacturer's instructions and store them at -20°C.
Prepare 200 ml of RPMI 1640 media supplemented with 11 mM glucose, 10% horse serum, 100 U/ml penicillin G and 100 μg/ml streptomycin.
Remove 25 ml of islet culture media using an electronic pipettor.
Place the removed 25 ml of islet culture media in a 50 ml conical tube.
Supplement the 25 ml of islet culture media with a final concentration of 0.2 mM EGTA to generate pre-assay media.
Isolate intact islets from a pre-selected strain, sex, age, and genotype of mice following a routine collagenase digestion of the pancreas.
Pool together islets from like samples.
Aliquot 40 islets into one well of a 96-well tissue culture plate in 200 µl of islet culture media.
Fill empty wells immediately adjacent to wells with islets with 200 µl sterile water to provide an evaporation buffer.
Culture islets in media overnight at 37 °C under an atmosphere of 95% air and 5% CO2.
Add pre-assay media to one aliquot of lyophilized COI-loaded PLGA microspheres such that the final concentration of COI is 10 ng/µl.
Sonicate the resuspended COI-loaded microspheres in an ice water bath for 10 min at 160 W with 10 sec long pulses at 4 °C.
Add the same volume of pre-assay media to an equal mass of lyophilized control PLGA microspheres.
Sonicate the resuspended control PLGA microspheres in an ice water bath for 10 min at 160 W with 10 sec long pulses at 4 °C.
Visually confirm microspheres are dispersed by pipetting 2 µl of resuspended microspheres between two glass coverslips.
Visualize microspheres using a 40X objective on an epifluorescence or brightfield microscope.
If significant aggregation of microspheres is visible, sonicate in an ice water bath for 10 min at 160 W with 10 sec long pulses at 4 °C and repeat visualization.
Prepare assay media by diluting resuspended COI microspheres to a final volume of 100 µl.
Prepare control assay media by diluting resuspended control PLGA microspheres with the same dilution volume used for COI-loaded microspheres.
Remove 100 μl of islet culture media from each well carefully without dislodging islets.
Add 100 μl of assay media or 100 μl of control assay media to each well gently.
Incubate islets at 37 °C under an atmosphere of 95% air and 5% CO2 for three days.
Use a micropipette to carefully remove and discard assay media from all wells.
Gently add 200 μl PBS to islets to wash them of the assay media.
Carefully remove and discard PBS with a micropipette.
Wash islets again with an additional 200 μl PBS.
Remove and discard PBS with a micropipette.
Add 100 µl of 0.025% trypsin, 2 mM EDTA solution.
Incubate at RT for 3 min.
Pipet islets in the trypsin-EDTA solution up and down every 2 min until islets are visually confirmed to be dispersed into single cells using a light microscope.
Transfer the entire volume of each well individually into labeled microcentrifuge tubes.
Add 400 µl of islet culture media to each microcentrifuge tube to stop the trypsin-mediated cell dissociation.
Centrifuge samples for 5 min at 100 x g at 4 °C to pellet islet cells to the bottom of microcentrifuge tubes.
Gently remove supernatant using a micropipette.
Resuspend pellet in 200 µl fresh islet culture media.
Using a cyto-centrifuge, centrifuge dissociated islets at 140 x g for 3 min onto charged microscope slides.
Air dry slides at RT for 10 min.
Draw a box around the dissociated islets with a hydrophobic marking pen.
Fix cells with 75 µl 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) at room temperature for 10 min.
Remove 4% PFA and gently wash cells in 75 µl PBS two times.
Permeabilize cells with 75 µl 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS for 10 min.
Wash cells with 75 µl PBS.
Prepare a humid chamber by placing two wet paper towels in the bottom of a 100 slide capacity microscope slide box.
Place slides flat down (cells facing up) in humid chamber.
Aspirate the PBS from the previous wash step using a micropipette and add 75 µl of blocking solution (5% Normal Donkey Serum (NDS) in PBS).
Incubate slides in blocking solution for 1 hr at room temperature.
Gently aspirate blocking solution using a micropipette and add 75 µl of primary antibody solution containing guinea pig anti-insulin and rabbit anti-Ki67 antibodies, diluted 1 µg/ml in 5% NDS in PBS.
Incubate slides with primary antibody solution at room temperature for 1 hr.
Gently aspirate primary antibody solution using a micropipette.
Rinse the cells with 75 µl PBS.
Aspirate PBS using a micropipette.
Rinse cells two more times, each time with 75 µL PBS.
Incubate each sample with 75 µl anti-guinea pig Cy5 secondary antibody and anti-rabbit Cy3 secondary antibody diluted to 2 µg/ml in blocking solution for 1 hr at RT.
Aspirate secondary antibody solution using a micropipette.
Incubate in 75 µl of 300 nM DAPI in PBS for 3 min at RT.
Aspirate DAPI using a micropipette.
Rinse in deionized water for 5 min.
Gently aspirate water from samples using a micropipette.
Spot a drop (roughly 100 µl) of fast-drying mounting solution containing antifade reagent on a glass coverslip.
Invert the microscope slide sample side down onto the mounting solution.
Gently press the coverslip against the slide using a pipet tip to remove bubbles.
Wipe away excess liquid with a soft cleaning tissue.
Allow coverslips to dry overnight at RT.
Manually count 3,000 insulin-positive cells per sample.
Count how many of the insulin-positive cells are also Ki67-positive.
Only count insulin-positive cells with a well-defined and clearly visible nucleus.
Calculate the percentage of proliferating β-cells for each sample by dividing the number of Ki67-positive/insulin-positive cells by the total number of insulin-positive cells and multiplying by 100.
Determine if a statistically significant difference in β-cell proliferation exists between control and experimental samples using a one-way ANOVA with commercially available statistical software.
